text.p: Following are the main stories in Ljubljana Wednesday morning newspapers:
- The parliament will take a vote on whether to confirm the new government line-up presumably in the middle of next week.
- The Federal Republic of Yugoslavia on Tuesday said it would not allow other states of the former Yugoslavia to have access to archives of the former federation that were stored mainly in Belgrade.

- Slovenian companies lost some $3.1 billion of property in other states of the former Yugoslavia after the federation broke up in 1991. Some 45 percent of the lost property is in Croatia, while 36 percent of it is in Serbia.
- Slovenians will have to pay personal tax of between 17 and 50 percent for all 1996 net earnings above 770,355 tolars ($5,000), the Finance Ministry said.
- A five-day fashion fair started in Ljubljana on Thursday.
- Parliamentary committees will hold hearings of new ministerial candidates later this week.
- Due to a higher number of court cases and many changes of legislation in the past couple of years, waiting periods at Slovenian district courts extend to up to five years, court statistics show.

- In spite of new Bank of Slovenia rules that are forcing international investors to open custodial accounts in order to trade in Slovenian shares, most foreigners have not decided to sell their shares in Slovenian companies.
